This river starts as snow in the Rocky Mountains.
It carves through seven states, and nearly fifteen hundred miles of desert.
It's the Colorado River, and over forty million people depend on it.
But zoom in on one place.
This is Hoover Dam, finished in nineteen thirty-six.
Its concrete wall holds back Lake Mead, the largest reservoir in America.
When it's full, it stores about nine trillion gallons of water.
Water rushes through those towers into turbines, making power for over a million people.
Then comes the hard part: dividing the river.
Seven states share it under a deal from nineteen twenty-two, and Mexico gets a cut too.
California gets the biggest share, four point four million acre-feet.
Arizona takes two point eight, and Nevada, home of Las Vegas, gets just point three.
Most of that water goes to farms, growing food for the whole country.
Drought has dropped Lake Mead by more than one hundred feet since the year two thousand.
The white bathtub rings on the canyon walls show where the water used to be.
Today, in most years, the Colorado River never even reaches the sea.
